topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional Therapies and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and the mechanisms, toxicity, and resistance profiles of systemic cytotoxic agents.

topics.label: Targeting Intrinsic Vulnerabilities and Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic biological vulnerabilities of cancer cells, such as hormone receptor reliance, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Small-Molecule Kinase Inhibitors and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, clinical design, and diverse molecular resistance mechanisms associated with small-molecule inhibitors targeting hyperactive oncogenic kinases.

topics.label: Antibody-Based Therapeutics and Targeted Delivery
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the use of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to specifically bind surface antigens and direct cytotoxicity to malignant cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and Cellular Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the evidence for tumor immunosurveillance and evaluate therapeutic approaches that re-engage or engineer T cells to eradicate cancer cells.

topics.label: Clinical Challenges, Progress, and Future Outlook
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overarching assessment of modern therapeutic challenges, historical gains in survival, and emerging directions for cancer management.
